clue.text: More than one buccaneer talks about island

indicators.note: about means the word for talks goes around the island letter

parts.note: to prate is to talk idly, so talks gives PRATES
I is the standard map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Seafarers of the old Caribbean chatter away about some island they have found.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for sea robbers, matching the clue's phrase for several buccaneers.

clue.text: Son coming into inheritance — no time to show niggardliness

indicators.note: no means the time letter is removed
coming into puts the son letter inside the inheritance word

parts.note: patrimony is property inherited from one's father

explanation.surface: A son comes into his inheritance but has no time for spending it: pure meanness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming into' looks like inheriting; it puts S inside PATRIMONY, then 'no time' removes the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme reluctance to spend money, a direct synonym for stinginess.

clue.text: Say nearly everyone will support rule of a monarch

indicators.note: will support means, in a down clue, the following letters sit underneath

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what say means here

indicators.note: nearly drops the last letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Nearly everybody will back a king's or queen's rule, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal, befitting or belonging to a king or queen.

clue.text: Reverie includes exclamation of support for play

indicators.note: includes means the reverie word holds the exclamation inside

parts.note: a trance is a dreamy state, a reverie
olé is the Spanish cheer of encouragement

explanation.surface: A daydream features a cheer for a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' is not drama but slack: the allowed movement in a mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineering sense: the permitted variation or free movement between parts.

clue.text: Exponent of magic more annoyed about church, right?

indicators.note: about means the annoyed word wraps around the church and right letters

parts.note: sorer means more aggrieved
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A conjuror grows crosser about the church, and who could blame them?
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard or practitioner of magic spells.

clue.text: Small thing in hat of no great size

indicators.note: in places the small thing inside the word for hat

parts.note: lid is informal slang for a hat or cap
a mite is a tiny creature or object

explanation.surface: Something tiny is tucked inside a hat that is itself rather small.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restricted in extent is modest in size, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Untrained person taking nothing away from curious anomaly

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are rearranged
taking away from means the nothing letter is subtracted from the word
with taking, says the nothing letter is subtracted

parts.note: O represents nothing, zero

explanation.surface: An amateur sees nothing odd in a strange irregularity.
explanation.walkthrough: ANOMALY loses an O and 'curious' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional with no specialist training, the everyday sense.

clue.text: Saw bum, not head, rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, reversed
not head drops the first letter

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction about a backside going up, minus its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun: a saying. BOTTOM loses its B, then 'rising' turns OTTOM round.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a meaning shared with a slogan.

clue.text: Boss has to lead, supported by a fool

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue puts the fool word beneath

parts.note: to top is to lead, as in topping a league
banana is informal for a silly person

explanation.surface: A boss has to take the lead while propped up by an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom for the person in charge, the chief.

clue.text: Italian leader adopting duke's scheme

indicators.note: adopting means the leader word takes the duke letter in

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler takes on a nobleman's plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgy trick or ruse, an informal synonym for a crafty plan.

clue.text: Half of your gallery trashed in a predictable way

indicators.note: trashed means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
half of picks the latter two of the four letters in your

explanation.surface: Vandals wreck part of a visitor's art gallery, as they seem to do with tedious frequency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes UR, the back half of 'your'; 'trashed' rearranges UR with GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at fixed, expected intervals means doing it predictably, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Little power in food regime — turned unenthusiastic

indicators.note: turned means the whole assembly is read backwards
in puts the power letter inside the food regime word

parts.note: a diet is a regime of eating
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone grows half-hearted about a diet that gives them little energy.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside DIET to make DIPET; 'turned' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm, literally and figuratively, so lacking keenness or warmth of feeling.

clue.text: Layabout left surrounded by booze, losing head

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the left letter inside the shortened drink
losing head drops the opening letter of the drink

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A lazy drinker is left slumped among the bottles, nursing a sore head.
explanation.walkthrough: CIDER loses its C to give IDER, and L goes inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is a lazy loafer, someone who does no work.

clue.text: English science facility charge will include nothing complicated

indicators.note: will include means the nothing letter sits within the facility-plus-charge pair

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is a place for science
a rate is a charge or fee
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An English laboratory's fees come with nothing included and baffling small print.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate and detailed is complicated, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Criminal bid involves murder

indicators.note: involves means the word for bid wraps around the word for murder

parts.note: an offer is a bid, as at auction
to end someone is to kill them

explanation.surface: A criminal's plan involves killing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker who commits a crime, the noun sense of criminal.

clue.text: Toilet had onset of wetness in autumn — this stops the flow

indicators.note: in places the toilet, had and wetness pieces inside the season word

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
loo is British informal for toilet
'd is the contraction of had

indicators.note: onset of takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A lavatory sprang a leak one autumn, and this is what holds back the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier built to hold back rising rivers or seas, so it halts water.

clue.text: Japanese ruler I'm backing with business involving King

indicators.note: involving puts the king letter within the reversed pronoun and the fuss word
backing means the letters of I'm are read in reverse

parts.note: ado is fuss or business, as in much ado
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An emperor backs a venture that involves another monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic title of the emperor of Japan, so a Japanese ruler.

clue.text: Spanish girl wrecked scene, basically

parts.note: Inés is a Spanish girl's name

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters are smashed and reordered

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl trashes the place, which is fundamentally what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentally, at its core; an adverbial idiom.

clue.text: Old writer inclined to ignore time, leaving nothing definite

parts.note: a pen writes

indicators.note: to ignore means the time letter is left out

parts.note: tended means inclined, as in tended to agree

explanation.surface: An old author, given to forgetting the time, leaves everything vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestricted or unresolved, so no fixed limits or conclusion are set.

clue.text: Demolished villa claimed by star composer

indicators.note: claimed by means the rebuilt letters are held within the star word

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: demolished means the word villa is knocked down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A celebrity composer had a villa demolished.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Sullivan composed the music for the Savoy operas with Gilbert.

clue.text: Arab country home to old farmers

indicators.note: home to means the country contains the old letter

parts.note: Yemen is an Arab country on the Arabian Peninsula

explanation.surface: An Arab nation is home to traditional farming folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically English freeholders who farmed their own land, so small farmers.

clue.text: Slow to block student producing work for Guardian

indicators.note: to block means the slow word sits inside the student word, obstructing it

parts.note: a tutee is a student taught by a tutor
to lag is to be slow, falling behind

explanation.surface: A slow learner gets in the way of a pupil writing a piece for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but means a protector or custodian.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardianship or instruction is the job of a protector, the custodial duty implied.

clue.text: Train inadequately, keeping United following old approaches

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the united letter
inadequately means the letters are done badly, so rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football coach trains United poorly, sticking to tired methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for stuck in a dull routine, unable to change habits.

clue.text: Mostly risking tucking into food for the purposes of health

indicators.note: tucking into means the shortened gambling word goes inside the food word

parts.note: a meal is food

indicators.note: mostly drops the last letter

parts.note: dicing, as in dicing with death, means risking

explanation.surface: Someone taking chances by tucking into food says it is all for their wellbeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having healing properties, so used for the sake of wellbeing and cure.

clue.text: Giant cat swallowing a gerbil's head

indicators.note: swallowing means the cat word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat

indicators.note: head takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A cat swallows a pet gerbil whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Gog and Magog are legendary giants, guardians of the City of London.

clue.text: Concern about daughter in political group

indicators.note: about means the concern word goes round the daughter letter

parts.note: care is concern

explanation.surface: Worry about a daughter who has joined a political faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A small core of trained activists within a party or movement.

clue.text: Occupied place that is for composer

parts.note: a person who sat occupied a place, as in a seat
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A seat taken, that is, for a composer at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, known for the Gymnopédies.

clue.text: Asian people: millions in the end

indicators.note: in places the millions letter inside the end word

parts.note: the tail is the end part
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Millions of Asian people at the end of a list.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethnic group of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Piano, it is admitted, missing penultimate note of scale

indicators.note: missing means the note is taken out

parts.note: granted means it is admitted or conceded
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, the one before doh returns

explanation.surface: A pianist concedes they skipped the second-last note of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A large concert piano with horizontal strings, often referred to by this word alone.

clue.text: Angry? I'm v angry, endlessly upset, notice

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged
endlessly drops the final letter

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone declares their fury at a notice, getting more worked up as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ANGRY to ANGR; 'upset' rearranges I'M, V and ANGR into RAVINGM.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious to the point of losing control, an informal intensified synonym.

clue.text: Writer recalled making three times as much — but name's forgotten

indicators.note: recalled means the remaining letters are called back, read in reverse
forgotten means the name letter is dropped

parts.note: trebling is making three times as much
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An author remembers tripling their earnings, though their name has slipped from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: TREBLING without N is TREBLIG; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert wrote the librettos for the Gilbert and Sullivan comic operas.

clue.text: Annoyed poverty was a governing factor

parts.note: need is want or poverty
led means guided or was in charge

explanation.surface: Someone resentful because hardship ruled their life.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated by repeated provocation, a past-participle synonym for irked.
